title: Show HN: Lossless-memory – a personal AI memory that never summarizes
text: Show HN: Lossless-memory – a personal AI memory that never summarizes type: news-summary · created: 2026-09-21 · updated: 2026-09-24 · confidence: high hacker-news Summary Lossless-memory is a personal AI memory system built on a refusal to summarize: most long-term memory systems either compress conversations into notes or embed and retrieve similar chunks, and both lose what actually matters to someone who talks to the same AI every day, what was actually said, and when. This project appends every conversation turn as a fixed seven-field record timestamp, actor, role, type, verbatim text, model, session to a per-day JSONL file; the raw logs are the source of truth and every index can be deleted and rebuilt from them. Time is the primary axis, not metadata: the AI can answer 'what did we decide last Tuesday night?' with the actual lines from last Tuesday night, in order. A tiny index of timestamped topic markers LLL , injected into the model's context every turn, lets a long-running assistant come back from compaction. The lineage runs from a December 2025 memory-inheritance tool through a predecessor in daily use since January 2026; this implementation has run every day since July 2026 for one user, with raw logs back to June 2026, and docs/lessons.md documents the failures. Highlights - Lossless-memory: personal AI memory that never summarizes; keeps every line with a timestamp. - Critique: summarization and embedding retrieval both lose what was actually said and when. - Seven-field record per turn: ts, actor, role, type, verbatim text, model, session; per-day JSONL files. - Raw logs are the source of truth; all indexes are rebuildable and disposable. - Time as primary axis: answer 'what did we decide last Tuesday night?' with the actual lines. - LLL: tiny timestamped topic-marker index injected into context every turn to survive compaction. - In daily use since July 2026 for one user; lineage back to December 2025; failures documented in docs/lessons.md. Source Read the original story https://github.com/aru-labs/lossless-memory Related pages No related entity or concept page yet.

title: OpenAI: 'fully autonomous RSI is not happening today'
text: OpenAI: 'fully autonomous RSI is not happening today' type: news-summary · created: 2026-09-21 · updated: 2026-09-24 · confidence: high techmeme openai ai-policy-regulation Summary OpenAI lays out its position on the next phase of AI development: as automated AI research takes over more of the work of building successive model generations, recursive self-improvement RSI could accelerate progress rapidly even while people remain involved. The company frames its mission around three goals - building an automated AI researcher while iterating on the alignment problem, delivering the economic benefits of very intelligent machines, and empowering individuals with a personal AGI - and argues alignment research must keep pace with capabilities. The post stresses that capable, aligned AI is itself part of the safety answer, strengthening defenses and advancing alignment research, and calls for shared standards to guide development across labs and countries. Notably, OpenAI states that fully autonomous RSI is 'not happening today', positioning gradual, supervised automation of research as the manageable path rather than an abrupt intelligence explosion. Highlights - OpenAI: fully autonomous recursive self-improvement RSI 'is not happening today' - Three stated goals: build an automated AI researcher and iterate on alignment; deliver scientific and economic benefits; empower everyone with a personal AGI - Warns that as AI drives more of its own R&D, the pace of progress could accelerate rapidly even with humans in the loop - Argues alignment research must keep pace with capabilities as systems grow more autonomous - Calls for shared standards to guide development across labs and countries - Frames capable, aligned AI as part of the defense against the risks of the transition itself Source Read the original story https://openai.com/index/building-standards-next-phase-ai/ Related pages OpenAI ../entities/openai.md · AI policy, regulation and litigation ../concepts/ai-policy-regulation.md
